payload.text: Texas A&M University | Texas A&M University Skip to Primary Navigation Skip to Main Content Celebrate 150 Years Faculty member Mark Benden overseeing innovative dementia research; close-ups of high-tech equipment and engaged faces in the lab. Engineering students collaborating intently on complex machinery in the RAD lab. Virtual Production Institute team producing immersive video content inside the iconic Kyle Field, creative energy in motion. Atmospheric sciences faculty and students clustered around glowing weather screens. A proud Texas A&M student, beaming, graduates and embraces her father and family, shining her new Aggie ring. Women’s volleyball team erupts in joyous celebration—trophy lifted high, confetti raining down. Aggie Wranglers dance team dazzles with dynamic spins. Beloved mascot Reveille in a candid, spirited campus moment. Veterinary students sharing a gentle moment, petting and caring for a horse. A mobile nurse carefully checks on a patient inside a vibrant BUILD container clinic. Visitors explore the George H.W. Bush Museum—snapshots of legacy and inspiration. Equestrian student, flag in hand. Members of the Aggie Corps salute. American flag flutters. Corps members lower and meticulously fold the flag. Together, we stand as A Force for Good pause At Texas A&M University, we develop leaders of character who take action and create lasting impact. Through educational excellence and world-class research, we are building a brighter, safer world for the people of Texas, the nation and beyond. Learn How to Apply Request Information View Colleges & Schools Visit Texas A&M Four-time Grammy Award winner Lyle Lovett (Texas A&M Class of ’79) grabs an acoustic guitar and walks to his porch to play as Aggie fans fill Kyle Field in red, white, and blue during a football game and members of the Fightin’ Texas Aggie Band march through campus. Aggies collaborate across classrooms, labs, and cockpits, exchanging high-fives and handshakes, followed by a doorman helping a young woman into a truck, veterinarians caring for animals, and students converting shipping containers into medical clinics. Scenes shift to Aggies working together in a robotics lab, on Capitol Hill, and on a ropes course, cutting back to Lyle Lovett playing on his porch while Aggies dance to country music. The Texas A&M volleyball team celebrates winning a national championship, followed by Aggies building racing vehicles, an Aggie-branded racecar winning on the track, the women’s tennis team winning a national championship, and graduation ceremonies that include the commissioning of military officers. Aggies fight wildfires, repair a pipe on a ship, test a robotic leg, receive their Aggie rings, and participate in local rodeos and parades, before members of the Corps of Cadets lower and fold the American flag, ending with the Texas A&M closing logo and brand text displayed on screen. Today, we are a research-intensive main university dedicated to sending leaders out into the world prepared to take on the challenges of tomorrow. Learn more about our university, including our goals, mission, values, locations, leadership and history. Frequently Asked Questions Academic Programs Texas A&M University Mission Statement Texas A&M University is dedicated to the discovery, development, communication, and application of knowledge in a wide range of academic and professional fields. Its mission of providing the highest quality undergraduate and graduate programs is inseparable from its mission of developing new understandings through research and creativity. It prepares students to assume roles in leadership, responsibility and service to society. Texas A&M assumes as its historic trust the maintenance of freedom of inquiry and an intellectual environment nurturing the human mind and spirit. It welcomes and seeks to serve persons of all racial, ethnic and geographic groups as it addresses the needs of an increasingly diverse population and a global economy. In the 21st century, Texas A&M University seeks to assume a place of preeminence among public universities while respecting its history and traditions. Facts about Texas A&M See university facts and statistics, including information about our rankings, research, employees, students and degree programs. What makes Texas A&M Distinct For nearly 150 years, Texas A&M University has set itself apart through its dedication to academic excellence and building strong leaders of character ready to make a mark on the world and demonstrate what it means to be a force for good. 1 of 24 institutions in the nation to hold the triple designation as a land-, sea- and space-grant university. Texas A&M Division of Research $22B in state economic impact. Texas A&M and the activities of its current and former students support 1 out of every 81 jobs in Texas. Lightcast , 2025 1 in 5 research dollars spent in Texas go to Texas A&M — nearly $1.4B in FY 2024 NSF , 2021 Fueling the Texas Economy. Securing the Nation The Texas A&M Maritime Academy is developing the next generation of maritime workers — the backbone of national security and economic strength. The future of earth and space runs through Texas Recognized for helping shape and equip principled leaders, Texas A&M recently welcomed the inaugural cohort of U.S. Space Force service members selected to participate in a four-week course.
